Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level answers below and I attached a short proposal and an Excel with three quant/batch scenarios. Quick TL;DR up front: for the profile you described I’d recommend a staged pilot (3 months) on a committed small Reserved pool + a 20% pilot credit and instrumenting caching to capture the short-chat ROI. That keeps latency low for chat and lets us tune aggressive 8-bit quantization on the long-run summarization jobs in parallel.

1) Pilot packaging recommendation
- Phase A (0–6 weeks): Reserved baseline (small pool) sized for 95th percentile chat concurrency; credit-backed burst for peak growth (configured as Dedicated burst lanes).
- Phase B (6–12 weeks): Introduce autoscale + prefix/KV caching for the summary ops; enable batching windows for high-throughput summarization.
- Operational guardrails: canary the 8-bit quantized variant behind the standard float model for 1k eval queries to watch for regressions.

2) Quantization guidance
- Chat (short sequences): 8-bit quantization (GPT-style symmetric quant) typically results in <1.5% drop in intent accuracy on conversational prompts for models we validate; recommended to keep 16-bit for top-K sensitive prompts.
- Summarization (longer sequences): start with 8-bit with calibration (per-layer clipping) for cost benefits, test on your 100-sample eval set; if you see >3% delta in rouge/faithfulness, fall back to 16-bit for the top-importance jobs.

3) Pricing / discounting posture for a ~$60k pilot
- Standard pilot offer: 20% credit on committed spend + 2 weeks free scaling to validate burst; does not require exec approval.
- If OpsLyte signs a Memorandum of Actioned (MA) pilot (3 months, $60k committed), we can increase to 30% effective discount by shifting 30% to an upfront refundable credit (requires AE sign-off; legal minimal redline).
- Anything >35% effective concession or multi-year price locks goes to Head of Sales approval.

Next steps: I can run these numbers against your sketch and put together a mutual action plan. I've attached OpsLyte_MAProposal_v2.pdf and quant-batching-scenarios.xlsx which contain the scenario costs and sample quantization test plan.

Would you be available Tues 2 Aug 10am PT? Priya — if you prefer a different time, send options and we’ll adapt.

Stephanie — quick internal note / suggested concessions before we share the MA:

- Approve the 20% pilot credit and the burst lane offer as standard — no escalation.
- If customer explicitly wants the 30% uplift (upfront refundable credit), require: signed pilot SOW, 30-day cancellation notice, and we cap custom SLA to pilot tier (no enterprise SLA). That keeps precedent tidy.
